name: Juba
subtitle: Juba, capital of South Sudan: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 368,436 people live in Juba County (counted 2008).
Juba grew from a mission station near a small Bari village on the White Nile; the site was chosen in 1927 as a new administrative headquarters (Mongalla Province) by Arthur Wallace Skrine.
Juba is the capital of Central Equatoria State and was the seat of the Government of Southern Sudan.

parts.text: Juba grew from a mission station near a small Bari village on the White Nile; the site was chosen in 1927 as a new administrative headquarters (Mongalla Province) by Arthur Wallace Skrine.
Juba is the capital of Central Equatoria State and was the seat of the Government of Southern Sudan.

Juba was chosen as capital of Southern Sudan partly as a gesture of inclusiveness, since it lies in Bari heartland; it already had an airport, water and was closer to neighbouring countries. Ram Chiel had been the favoured option.
South Sudan declared independence on 9 July 2011, with celebrations in Juba.
Plans exist to move the capital to Ramciel; in 2017 South Sudan signed an agreement with Morocco for construction there, with no clear start date.

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in Juba County?

parts.text: 368,436 in 2008, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Juba County (not the city alone), census of 22 April 2008, as relayed by citypopulation.de from the South Sudan National Bureau of Statistics.

items.text: Arthur Wallace Skrine chooses the Juba site as new administrative headquarters.
Juba becomes capital of the Southern Sudan regional government, with about 10,600 people (ODI's wording).
During the second civil war Juba is a garrison town under the Government of Sudan.
When the Comprehensive Peace Agreement is signed, Juba is home to about 250,000 people including 87,000 IDPs (ODI estimate).
Independence celebrated in Juba; a statue honouring Garang and the war dead is unveiled at the mausoleum.
Agreement with Morocco for building the planned new capital at Ramciel.
Opening ceremony of the Freedom Bridge over the Nile in Juba.
